code.text: Progressive weakness and loss of coordination for about a year: fumbling with buttons and a bat, tripping on curbs, a fall on the ice in the winter, muscle cramps and twitching in the arms and thighs; no numbness, pain, double vision, or trouble speaking or swallowing. Examination: wasting of the hand muscles (left more than right), fasciculations in both arms and thighs, weakness of grip and of left ankle dorsiflexion, brisk reflexes with spread and a positive Hoffmann sign, normal sensation. Mixed upper and lower motor neuron signs; evaluation for motor neuron disease and its mimics begun, with neuromuscular neurology consultation booked

note.text: Synthetic teaching-case problem. Evidence grade S. Historical claims: CLM-0004, CLM-0005, CLM-0011.

code.text: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, limb onset: progressive weakness for about a year with upper and lower motor neuron signs in the cervical and lumbosacral regions, and active and chronic denervation on EMG in the cervical, thoracic and lumbosacral regions with normal sensory nerve conduction; MRI of the brain and cervical spine and blood tests exclude mimics. Meets the Gold Coast criteria and the revised El Escorial category of clinically probable ALS. ALSFRS-R 42 and FVC 88% of predicted at diagnosis. Synthetic modern episode linked to his documented diagnosis

text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Evaluation of progressive weakness with mixed upper and lower motor neuron signs: blood count, metabolic panel with calcium, creatine kinase, vitamin B12, TSH, A1c, serum protein electrophoresis with immunofixation, and an HIV test; MRI of the brain and cervical spine; seated spirometry
  • Neuromuscular neurology consultation with EMG and nerve conduction studies for progressive weakness with mixed upper and lower motor neuron signs
  • Safety while the evaluation proceeds: no competitive play or heavy lifting, a physical therapy assessment of balance and gait, home fall precautions (night lights, rails, no loose rugs), and a same-day call for any trouble swallowing or breathing; results given to him first, in person
  • Riluzole 50 mg twice daily, with ALT monthly for the first 3 months and then every 3 months, and a blood count with any fever; genetic testing with genetic counseling for ALS-associated genes, with tofersen only if an SOD1 variant is found; edaravone discussed as an option with modest evidence in a selected group
  • Multidisciplinary ALS clinic every 2 to 3 months (neurology, nursing, physical, occupational and speech therapy, nutrition, respiratory therapy, social work and mental health): ALSFRS-R, seated forced vital capacity and maximal inspiratory pressure, and weight at every visit; cognitive and behavioral screening; PHQ-9
  • Respiratory plan: forced vital capacity and maximal inspiratory pressure every visit, supine capacity and overnight oximetry when values fall or symptoms appear; noninvasive ventilation when forced vital capacity is below 50% of predicted, maximal inspiratory pressure is weaker than -60 cmH2O, overnight oximetry shows desaturation, or orthopnea or morning headaches appear; influenza and COVID-19 vaccines
  • Nutrition, speech, swallowing and mobility: a high-calorie diet to keep weight stable, with gastrostomy discussed early, while forced vital capacity is above 50%; speech and swallowing assessments every visit and voice banking; a left ankle-foot orthosis, a cane, and an early power wheelchair evaluation because of lead times; home and car adaptations
  • Work and planning: workplace accommodations for a desk role (accessible office, flexible hours, rest breaks, voice-recognition software, parking), information on disability benefits, social work support, and early advance care planning, revisited at each change

resource.title: Lou Gehrig synthetic care plan
resource.description: Primary care for a 35-year-old professional baseball player with a year of progressive weakness and loss of coordination: recognizing mixed upper and lower motor neuron signs, excluding mimics (MRI of the brain and cervical spine, blood tests, EMG and nerve conduction studies), and making the diagnosis of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis on the Gold Coast and revised El Escorial criteria; riluzole with liver test monitoring, genetic testing (tofersen only for an SOD1 variant) and edaravone discussed; a multidisciplinary ALS clinic tracking ALSFRS-R, forced vital capacity and weight; nutrition, speech and swallowing, mobility equipment, noninvasive ventilation thresholds, work accommodation, mood screening, and early advance care planning, on the AAN ALS practice parameters (1922).
